newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angolan govt supporting Zaire rebels - diplomats.
newsitem.headline: Angolan govt supporting Zaire rebels - diplomats.

text.p: The Angolan government is sending exiled Zairean Katangese rebels back home to join in the fight to overthrow veteran President Mobutu Seso Seko, diplomatic sources said on Friday.
"We all know that the government has sent the Katangese back to Zaire to fight with the rebels," said an African diplomat who asked not to be identified.
"The Angolan government may be saying publicly they do not have any troops in Zaire, but the fact is they are flying transport planes with these Katangese aboard out of bases around Luanda to Zaire."

Angolan army spokesman Brigadier Jose Manuel Jota denied any Angolan involvement in the Zairean fighting, where rebels have taken control of at least one-fifth of the country after a campaign starting last October.

The Katangese rebels fought failed secessionist wars in Zaire's southern Shaba province against Mobutu in the 1960s and 1970s. Many left for Angola after they were defeated, where some joined the military.
"There are a number of Angolan military units made up entirely of Katangese. These are the ones who have been sent over to help out the rebels," another African diplomat said.

Western diplomats said a number of senior Angolan government officials, while outwardly denying any involvement in the Zairean conflict, were supporting the rebels who have been fighting in the east of the country since October last year.
They said the strife was seen as an opportunity to strike back at Mobutu for his support of parties opposed to the Angolan government.

"Several people in the Angolan military have come to us and said there is this group in the upper circles of the government and in the military that want to punish Zaire for its past support of the FNLA (National Front for the Liberation of Angola) and UNITA," one diplomat said.
The FNLA was an early independence group and UNITA a rebel movement which fought a long civil war against the government.
Diplomats and military analysts in Luanda estimate that Kantagese living in Angola number "in the thousands".

One diplomat said flights had initially left from Luanda but were later moved to an airbase south of the city called Cabo Ledo. Another diplomat said Katangese had also been moved back to Zaire from a government base at Saurimo, in Lunda Sul Province.
